chunks: For everything there is a limit (hadd), and whoever exceeds that limit, there shall be a penalty (hadd) upon him.

key_terms.تَعَدَّى: To transgress, exceed, or go beyond the defined limit
key_terms.حَدّ (limit): Boundary or limit set by divine law, demarcating what is permitted
key_terms.حَدّ (punishment): Prescribed legal penalty (hadd punishment) for those who transgress the limit

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about limits and penalties in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a foundational principle of Islamic jurisprudence: every permissible or obligatory matter has defined limits established by divine law, and transgressing those limits incurs prescribed legal penalties. The Arabic term 'hadd' (حَدّ) carries a deliberate double meaning — first as a boundary set by God, and second as the prescribed legal punishment (hadd punishments) for those who violate it. This teaching grounds the jurisprudential concept that divine legislation is precise and bounded, and that legal accountability follows transgression.
